FIRST ALERT: Severe storms possible in Texas Panhandle Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday

By Jayden Ramkissoon and Shelden Breshears
Published: Oct. 11, 2026 at 8:23 PM EDT|Updated: 11 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:45
Instaread

AMARILLO, Texas (KFDA) - Severe thunderstorms are still on track to impact at least parts of the Texas Panhandle going into this afternoon and evening.

The general set up right now really hinges on where prime lift can meet up with the best moisture as drier air intrudes from the west. Any rain we get in our area may get a little boost from hurricane Simon from the south.

Thunderstorms look to begin to fire up right around Amarillo, and areas off to the eastern half of the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles. A timeline is below:

Amarillo and areas to the east are under a slight risk for severe thunderstorms Tuesday afternoon and evening.

Damaging winds and large hail are the main threats, with gusts over 60 mph and hail as large as ping-pong balls possible. The tornado risk is very low, but not zero, so we’ll stay vigilant for all threats.

Be sure to track along with the First Alert Weather team as we stream continuous updates and information on our website and streaming platforms.

Going into Wednesday, we may see some thunderstorm chances for the first half of the day. These chances will likely have more of a localized flooding impact, with lower severe threats before the system moves out with a cold front by Thursday.
